newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian Shi'ites Moslems protest arrests.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian Shi'ites Moslems protest arrests.

text.p: Thousands of Shi'ite Moslems protesting the arrest of their leaders took to the streets in northern Nigeria on Friday, residents of the area said on Saturday.
"The demonstration was peaceful but the police also acted swiftly by rolling out anti-riot tanks," said a radio journalist from Kaduna, the headquarters of the north.

The mainly Moslem north has been the scene of religious riots several times, most recently last month when three people were killed in a clash between rival Moslem sects in Kano, the most populous city in the north.
Local newspapers reported that Friday's protest took place in Kaduna and Katsina and followed the arrest on Thursday of the Shi'ite leader named as Ibrahim Yaqub El-Zak-Zaky.
The Guardian newspaper said the protesters, dressed in black and red, marched orderly through main roads handing out handbills titled "Where is El-Zak-Zaky?"

A statement by the sect said El-Zak-Zaky and other leaders of the group were arrested by police and taken to an unknown destination after clashes between the sect and Christians in the town of Kafanchan, south of Kaduna.
Kaduna state's new military administrator Lieutenant-Colonel Hammed Ibrahim Ali vowed that hard times awaited trouble makers in the state.

"If you forment trouble in the name of religion I will get on your back and when I do that nobody can save you," Ali was quoted as telling the people of the state during a tour of rural areas on Friday.
Residents of Kaduna said the city was calm on Saturday.
